questions.q: What is a Docker image, according to this lesson?
options: A read-only template — a filesystem snapshot plus a startup command — built once from a Dockerfile
A running, writable instance of a container
A single compressed file with no internal structure
A virtual machine disk image
questions.explain: The image is the read-only recipe; the container is a running instance of it with its own writable layer.

questions.q: If you run `docker run my-ai-app` three times, what happens?
options: Three separate images are built
The second and third runs fail because the image is already in use
The image is modified by each container
One image produces three independent, isolated containers
questions.explain: One built image can be started as a container any number of times; each container is independent and disposable.

questions.q: What happens to the underlying image when a container built from it is stopped?
options: The image is deleted along with the container
The image is rolled back to its previous version
The image is untouched — only the container's writable layer disappears
The image's digest changes
questions.explain: A container's writable layer is disposable; the read-only image underneath is unaffected by stopping or removing the container.

questions.q: In the Docker Desktop image-inspector screenshot, what do tabs like Packages, Base images, and Vulnerabilities actually describe?
options: Live network traffic from a running container
Settings for the Docker Engine as a whole
A list of other users' containers
Properties of the built image itself, true whether or not a container is currently running from it
questions.explain: Those tabs show facts about the image — its packages, base image, and known vulnerabilities — independent of any running container.

questions.q: What does the Docker Hub browse page screenshot in this lesson illustrate?
options: A container actively running in production
The Docker Engine's source code repository
Images sitting in a registry, versioned and shared, before anything pulls and runs them
A billing dashboard for Docker subscriptions
questions.explain: Docker Hub is a registry — Lesson 6's topic — where built images wait until something pulls them down and starts them as containers.
